react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in the treatment group. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) and SMPDB:SMP00356 (17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency) as joint top hits with an FDR of 6.05e-18, each driven by six overlapping C18-C19 steroid compounds. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-only PSEA recovers KEGG:hsa00140 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the sole significant hit with a p-value of 5.77e-07, involving the identical six steroids. Mummichog m/z-direct activity ranks MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism first (p=8.40e-05, 15 compounds) and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism second (p=7.56e-04, 14 compounds). The six driver metabolites — 17β-estradiol (C00951), estrone (C00468), androstenedione (C00280), testosterone (C00535), dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), and dihydrotestosterone (C03917) — occupy central positions in both the androgen and the estrogen arms of these pathways. N-acetylgalactosamine (C01074) hits only the glycan-degradation mummichog subnetworks, while coumarin (C05851) and xanthine (C00385) are absent from every steroid enrichment result.

payload_summary.fallback_suggested: use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead
